subject: math
cluster: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume

items.prompt: Find the area of a rectangle with length $13\text{ cm}$ and width $6\text{ cm}$.

steps: Use the rectangle area formula $A=bh$, where $b$ is the length and $h$ is the width.
Area is measured in square units, so $A=78\text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: Find the area of a triangle with base $14\text{ cm}$ and height $9\text{ cm}$.

steps: Area uses square units, so $A=63\text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A parallelogram has base $11\text{ in}$ and height $7\text{ in}$. Find its area.

steps: Use the parallelogram area formula $A=bh$, where $h$ is the perpendicular height.
Area uses square units, so $A=77\text{ in}^2$.

items.prompt: Find the volume of a cube with edge length $5\text{ cm}$.

steps: A cube has all edges equal, so its volume is $V=s^3$.
Volume uses cubic units, so $V=125\text{ cm}^3$.

items.prompt: Find the volume of a rectangular prism that is $8\text{ m}$ long, $4\text{ m}$ wide, and $3\text{ m}$ tall.

steps: Use $V=Bh$ where the base area is $B=\text{length}\times\text{width}$.
Volume uses cubic units, so $V=96\text{ m}^3$.

items.prompt: A trapezoid has parallel sides $b_1=10\text{ in}$ and $b_2=6\text{ in}$ and height $h=4\text{ in}$. Find its area.

steps: Area uses square units, so $A=32\text{ in}^2$.

items.prompt: A figure is a $12\text{ m}$ by $5\text{ m}$ rectangle with a triangle of base $12\text{ m}$ and height $4\text{ m}$ attached on top, like a house outline. Find the total area.

steps: Decompose the figure into a rectangle and a triangle, then add the areas.

items.prompt: A $9\text{ ft}$ by $9\text{ ft}$ square has a $4\text{ ft}$ by $3\text{ ft}$ rectangular hole cut out of it. Find the remaining area.

steps: Find the area of the full square: $A_{\text{square}}=9\times 9=81\text{ ft}^2$.
Find the area of the rectangular hole: $A_{\text{hole}}=4\times 3=12\text{ ft}^2$.
Subtract the hole from the square: $A=81-12=69$.

items.prompt: A triangular prism has a triangular base with area $B=18\text{ cm}^2$ and a length of $10\text{ cm}$. Find its volume.

steps: Use $V=Bh$, where $B$ is the area of the triangular base and $h$ is the length of the prism.
Volume uses cubic units, so $V=180\text{ cm}^3$.

items.prompt: A rectangular box measures $8\text{ cm}$ by $5\text{ cm}$ by $3\text{ cm}$. Find its surface area.

steps: A rectangular prism has three pairs of matching faces, so $SA=2(lw)+2(lh)+2(wh)$.
Surface area uses square units, so $SA=158\text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A parallelogram-shaped garden has an area of $48\text{ m}^2$ and a base of $8\text{ m}$. Find its height.

steps: Start from the area formula $A=bh$ and solve for the height $h=\frac{A}{b}$.
Height is a length, so $h=6\text{ m}$.

items.prompt: A triangular prism has a triangular base with base $6\text{ cm}$ and height $4\text{ cm}$. The prism is $9\text{ cm}$ long. Find its volume.

steps: First find the area of the triangular base using $B=\frac{1}{2}bh$.
Use $V=Bh$ with the prism length as the height: $V=12\times 9$.
Volume uses cubic units, so $V=108\text{ cm}^3$.

items.prompt: A room floor is shaped like an L. It is made of a $6\text{ ft}$ by $10\text{ ft}$ rectangle joined to a $4\text{ ft}$ by $5\text{ ft}$ rectangle, with no overlap. New tile costs $\$3$ per square foot. Find the total cost to tile the floor.

steps: Decompose the L-shape into two rectangles and add their areas.
Multiply the area by the cost per square foot: $80\times \$3=\$240$.

items.prompt: A gift box is a rectangular prism $20\text{ cm}$ long, $15\text{ cm}$ wide, and $10\text{ cm}$ tall. How many square centimeters of wrapping paper are needed to cover all six faces exactly once (ignore overlap)?

steps: Covering all six faces is the surface area: $SA=2(lw)+2(lh)+2(wh)$.
You need $1300\text{ cm}^2$ of wrapping paper.

items.prompt: A box-shaped aquarium is $80\text{ cm}$ long, $40\text{ cm}$ wide, and $50\text{ cm}$ tall. It is filled with water to a depth of $40\text{ cm}$. Given that $1000\text{ cm}^3$ of water equals $1$ liter, how many liters of water are in the aquarium?

steps: Only the filled portion holds water, so use the water depth of $40\text{ cm}$ as the height, not the full $50\text{ cm}$.
Find the volume of water with $V=Bh$, where $B$ is the base area: $B=80\times 40=3200\text{ cm}^2$.
Multiply by the water depth: $V=3200\times 40=128000\text{ cm}^3$.
Convert to liters by dividing by $1000$: $128000\div 1000=128$.
The aquarium holds $128$ liters of water.
